calculations.note: Transient resistor-only bounds assume a discharged gate and ideal source; actual driver/gate dynamics unmeasured. ST VOH drop at 3mA gives an upper driver-resistance bound, not a lower bound.

findings.evidence: The PC14 source cell states a gate-charge edge current <= about 2.9 mA by adding about 133 ohm driver resistance, obtained from 0.4 V / 3 mA, to R162=1 kohm. ST specifies at most 0.4 V output drop at 3 mA. Even a linear interpretation makes 133.3 ohm an upper resistance bound at that operating point, not a guaranteed minimum. The inequality therefore cannot establish the claimed upper current bound. Native R162 is 0805W8F1001T5E/C17513, 1 kohm +/-1%, between BUZZ_DRV and BUZZ_G; R163=10 kohm goes to GND.
findings.fix: Remove the <=2.9 mA proof from the pin-table source cell. Use the resistor-only nominal 3.3 mA upper bound (3.364 mA for the stated 3.33 V/990 ohm corner, before temperature/transients), label gate dynamics unmeasured, and regenerate pin-table/binding provenance. If a <=3 mA hardware design target is intended, choose a resistor minimum >=VDDmax/3mA and requalify the buzzer edge; do not infer it from VOH.
findings.impact: Bounded evidence error. No buzzer failure or absolute-maximum violation is demonstrated. The 3 mA row is an output-level characterization condition, not itself a newly proved hard transient-current maximum.
findings.title: PC14 current estimate reverses the driver-resistance bound

residuals_not_new_proven_defects.evidence: J410.1 and J420.1 both join PORT_4V8; no GPS/radio isolation or supply switch exists. The four UARTs go through1k only plus wire-to-GND ESD. Self-powered-port operation with board off is excluded; no resistor-only isolation claim is made.
The exact EL product page gives a15V working magnitude/48V typical16A TLP clamp; this does not establish a receiving-pin voltage. Installed cable ESD remains unqualified as already stated.

PB12/PB13 FT_u use VDD for UART operation by Table9 note7; PC6/PC7 are FT_h. Table112 operating conditions and supply-dependent limits must be respected in addition to absolute Table109; keep pulls disabled whenever the endpoint exceeds its relevant supply+0.3V. Normal0-5V endpoints are conditional on live supplies/configuration. No applied above-limit endpoint is demonstrated.

PC1 and PE4 share one MCU and must remain locked low around loader/debug transitions; actual trace override behavior remains untested. Latest AN2606 pin usage is consistent with the recorded old-version containment.
PA6/PB1 single-component-fault damage limits remain as recorded. These are not the protected pyro divider contract. No new normal-condition violation found.
